drivers.why_material: Safety framing for the catalyst program is refuted: the company asserted 'well-tolerated across all studies' while NCT06425159 (part of the opakalim epilepsy program) was terminated early with only 27 of 242 planned enrollments, and the catalyst trial NCT06132893 underwent a major protocol amendment adding safety co-primaries to Part A—both events signal safety concerns that contradict the 'well-tolerated' narrative filed just before the catalyst readout.

The company claimed 'on track' for 2H 2026 results on the catalyst trial NCT06132893 while the registered primary completion date had slipped 16 months (from August 2025 to December 2026) and stood at December 2026 as of the claim date—asserting 'on track' with a guidance that does not match the registry is operational masking for this specific catalyst.
Duplicate operational masking: again claims 'on track' for 2H 2026 results despite the catalyst trial's 16-month completion-date slip to December 2026, filed immediately before the catalyst.

dismissed.why_not_material: This claim (filed November 2025) referenced 1H 2026 results and appears to have concerned NCT06309966, which at the time had a registered completion of January 2026; the subsequent slip to May 2026 occurred after the claim, so the claim was not masking at the time it was made.

Cross-trial tolerability comparison is normal promotional context for an early-stage program; it does not mask the catalyst trial's own design or data, which is placebo-controlled and will stand on its own merits.

Cross-trial efficacy comparison to azetukalner is standard competitive positioning in investor materials; the catalyst trial is randomized and placebo-controlled, so this comparison does not misrepresent the basis of the upcoming readout.
Cross-trial safety comparison is promotional color based on open-label extension data; it does not mask the catalyst trial's controlled design or suggest manipulation of the pivotal endpoint.

analyst_note: Three material findings converge on the catalyst trial itself. First, the company claimed opakalim was 'well-tolerated across all studies' in late May 2026, yet one epilepsy trial (NCT06425159) was terminated early with only 11% of planned enrollment, and the catalyst trial (NCT06132893) underwent a major protocol amendment adding safety co-primaries—both inconsistent with the 'well-tolerated' narrative. Second, the company repeatedly asserted results were 'on track' for 2H 2026 while the registered primary completion date for NCT06132893 had slipped 16 months to December 2026 and remained there as of the claim dates. These are not cross-program issues (principle 2) but direct misrepresentations of the catalyst trial's safety profile and timeline. The cross-trial competitive comparisons (claims 8, 13, 22) are dismissed as normal IR color. The pattern of safety and operational masking on the catalyst trial warrants elevated caution, though there is no company-level fraud history (principle 1) to escalate to EXCLUDE.
